gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Elite 200 V2's 1,000 W solar ceiling (60 V open-circuit, 20 A) needs the panels to run at 50 V or more at the full 20 A (1,000 W ÷ 20 A). That is within 10 V of the 60 V cut-off, so the '1,000 W for future upgrades' in ChatGPT's answer is a best case and not something you get by adding more of the kit's own 200 W panels.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), Eco Solar Kits (cited) and Dealectric's own two pages; OutageReady (cited) could not be opened because of a certificate error. StormWatts already has the main fit check: Elite 200 V2 at 12–60 V and 20 A, SP200L at 24.6 V Voc and 10.8 A Isc, two in series at about 49 V (about 56.5 V on a −4°F morning), two in parallel at 21.6 A on a 20 A input. It also covers the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2's 400 W cap ('The 2 × 200W kit already reaches that cap') and the DELTA 3 Max's 60 V / 18 A limits at 88% of its 500 W input. Eco Solar Kits already says Power Lifting runs resistive loads up to 3,900 W at reduced voltage and 'is not a motor surge rating'. No rival does the 1,000 W ÷ 20 A = 50 V arithmetic. None covers how the two 350 W panels in the Elite 200 V2 + 2× 350 W kit must be wired either.
decides: This confirms the pick and does not change it. All three 2× panel kits ChatGPT showed work as shipped. The Elite 200 V2's two 200 W panels must be wired in series (about 49 V, under the 60 V limit), not in parallel. The Jackery 2000 v2 kit already uses its whole 400 W solar input, so it has no room to grow on solar. The DELTA 3 Max kit uses 440 W of its 500 W. The Elite 200 V2 has the most room to add panels, but it is a pre-order: dispatch Nov 26, 2026, per our 2026-11-17 store read. The page should therefore name a kit that ships now as the pick and give the Elite 200 V2 2× 200 W kit as the choice for a shopper who can wait and wants to add solar later. Its realistic solar ceiling is set by the 20 A input, not the 1,000 W headline.
candidates: Jackery Solar Generator 2000 v2 + 2× SolarSaga 200 W
